answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy tracking ivory cargo, basalt deposits, and botanical garden sensors uses verifiable delay functions. Each node must evaluate non-parallelizable sequential hashes, pacing identity creation cryptographically. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated single-core computation time and electrical energy per identity. However, this latency stalls honest nodes needing rapid onboarding and weakens against adversaries using custom high-speed ASICs.
